author: val
body: The timezone file on the ESP root. CTZ1 is eight bytes: 0..3 magic 'C' 'T' 'Z' '1'; 4 the hour offset plus twelve; 5..7 zero. CTZ2 is sixteen bytes whose first eight are byte for byte CTZ1 (same magic), so a CTZ1 reader still gets the whole-hour zone and a CTZ2 reader treats a short file as CTZ1: 8..9 offset in MINUTES plus 720, little endian; 10..11 zone id, little endian, 0 meaning offset only; 12 clock format; 13 date format; 14 the taskbar's display bits stored plus one (zero means a build that never wrote it); 15 zero. Offsets are biased because a byte read back is unsigned: a stored -5 returns 251.

author: val
body: The offset is a DISPLAY offset and is never written to the MC146818, which keeps UTC. A stick with no timezone answers UTC.
